question.problem: If $7{log}_{5}⁡x-2{log}_{5}⁡x=10$, then what is the value of  $x?$
question.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange our equation to isolate the logarithmic term:

$$
\begin{aligned}7{log}_{5}⁡x-2{log}_{5}⁡x & =10 \\ (7-2){log}_{5}⁡x & =10 \\ 5{log}_{5}⁡x & =10 \\ {log}_{5}⁡x & =2\end{aligned}
$$

To remove the logarithm, we exponentiate both sides of the equation. The base of the logarithm is $5,$ so we use this base for the exponentiation as well:

$$
\begin{aligned}{log}_{5}⁡x & =2 \\ {5}^{{log}_{5}⁡x} & ={5}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since exponentiation is the inverse function of the logarithm, we get ${5}^{{log}_{5}⁡x}=x.$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={5}^{2} \\ x & =25.\end{aligned}
$$
